instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: The 9/11 attacks did not have any social consequences for people in the USA.

wrong.text: For example, American Muslims had to deal with hate crimes or discrimination.

atoms.a: The 9/11 attacks affected the global standing of the USA.
In the last decades, crime rates increased in the USA.

wrong.text: From 1992 to 2022 crime rates decreased, but they are still high compared to rates in Europe.

atoms.a: In the USA, the death penalty is illegal.

wrong.text: It is legal in 27 USA states.

atoms.a: Today, limitations for the death penalty exist.
Opponents of the death penalty argue that it reinforces a culture of violence.
Opponents of the death penalty argue that criminals deserve death as a punishment.

wrong.text: This is an argument of those who advocate the death penalty.

atoms.a: The Second Amendment prohibits people from keeping arms.

wrong.text: It gives people the right to keep arms.

atoms.a: The large amount of gun-related deaths is an argument for stricter gun control.
The right to keep and bear arms cannot easily be changed by laws.
Mass shootings in the USA happen once a month.

wrong.text: There is almost one mass shooting per day.

atoms.a: After a mass shooting, the shooter often commits suicide.
When the shooter attacks many people, they are normally friends or colleagues.

wrong.text: They often have no relationship with each other.

atoms.a: A contributing cause to mass shootings is the copycat effect.
